title: Make recovery capacity part of the execution path
caption: The exception-budget control plane adds a capacity gate to the write path while keeping authorization independent.

title: Unknown is a durable state, not a retry instruction
caption: A lost response enters a durable unresolved state. Cancellation, retry and settlement each require a distinct proof.

title: Build the metric denominator before the dashboard
caption: A metric architecture keeps the business-action denominator separate from attempts, source events and deduplicated investigations.

title: Reserve capacity atomically, before granting dispatch
caption: Atomic reservations prevent concurrent overspend; they cannot eliminate forecast error or authorize unsafe work.

title: Keep authority shorter-lived than the workflow
caption: Leased authority and recovery ownership have different lifecycles. A compensation needs its own current authorization.

title: Commit the action once; reconcile the missing response
caption: The sequence identifies the local atomic boundary, lost-response branch and separate downstream-effect contracts.

title: Verification needs evidence independent of the agent
caption: Verification links an approved postcondition to authoritative evidence without using the agent narrative as its own proof.

title: Design human recovery as a finite service system
caption: The recovery architecture exposes staffing, skill constraints and the separate authorization of corrective actions.

title: Throttle the affected capability, preserve recovery
caption: Capability-scoped backpressure has explicit hold, recovery and reentry behavior, with hard safety stops outside the capacity budget.

title: Prove the failure paths before increasing autonomy
caption: Failure injection and bounded canaries test the real enforcement boundary and recovery burden before raising admission limits.

title: A 1% exception rate can exceed the recovery budget
caption: Scenario demand exceeds daily service capacity at 1%. Wilson uncertainty lowers the illustrative planning cap from 6,000 to 4,939 actions/day.

title: Queueing delay accelerates before full utilization
caption: Waiting time grows nonlinearly as utilization approaches one. The model is a continuous-service benchmark, not a forecast of calendar waiting time.
